label: verify-t2-patterns-lay

claims.claim: Chemotaxis along self-generated attractant gradients lets E. coli expand faster than unguided growth-plus-wandering (Cremer 2019).
claims.source_says: Low levels of chemoattractants act as aroma-like cues in this process, establishing the direction and enhancing the speed of population movement along the self-generated attractant gradients.
claims.note: Europe PMC abstract confirms the sentence (fetch returned the first part verbatim and paraphrased the rest); the 'faster than Fisher' comparison is implied by 'enhancing the speed'.

claims.claim: Narla 2021: speed grows with sqrt of growth rate and of relative attractant level, and does not depend on uptake rate.
claims.source_says: square root dependence on the growth rate r; further increased by the square root of the relative background attractant concentration, a0/am; the expansion speed c does not depend on the specific rate of attractant uptake μ
claims.note: All three dependences found in the Europe PMC full text of PMC8640786.

claims.claim: Square-root-of-growth baseline fitted on six wild-type rows (k=16.904) leaves only 7 of 17 other conditions within 15%, errors 7.8 to 94.0%.
claims.source_says: Recomputed from MOESM11.xlsx: k=16.9035, 17 held-out aspartate/serine rows, errors 7.81 to 93.97 percent, 7 within 15 percent; fit rows -9.6 to +11.1 percent.
claims.note: Arithmetic reproduces exactly; 'six wild-type rows' are the first six aspartate rows, as stated.

claims.claim: Law set 1.8.1 has no chemotaxis law; fisher-kpp-speed 1.1.0 is a candidate and non-binding.
claims.source_says: law_id fisher-kpp-speed, version 1.1.0, status candidate; note: 'the four genuine discovery candidates (turing-ddi, kimura-heterozygosity, maynardsmith-hawk-dove, fisher-kpp-speed) stay candidate and stay non-binding.'
claims.note: grep for chemotax/Keller in registry laws and lawsets returned no hits.

overall: All four key claims check out against the sources. Two were cited with slightly shortened quotes in the fetch tool, but the full wording matches.
